subject: Larkspur platform incident — consolidated post-incident commitments and timeline
messages:
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
To: Samira Khan <samira.khan@larkspur.ai>
Cc: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-01T10:12:00-07:00
Subject: Interim findings on April 28th latency spike + immediate next steps

Hi Samira,

Thank you again for the patience while our team investigated the service degradation you saw on April 28 (approx 02:14 UTC). I wanted to share our interim findings and the short list of immediate mitigations we applied so you have clarity while we complete the full postmortem.

What happened (interim summary)
- Impact: 5–15s median request latency increase and ~1.8% elevated 5xx rate for ~36 minutes across your dedicated pool. No requests were returned with user-visible data corruption.
- Preliminary root cause: a cache-consistency failure in our KV prefix cache tied to worker reallocation during an autoscaler reclaim operation. When a worker was removed and another worker picked up the same model shard, a race caused stale KV prefixes to be used for a short window.

Immediate actions we took (done)
- Temporarily disabled fast reclaim in the affected Dedicated pool to prevent further mid-roll evictions.
- Forced a coordinated drain+rehash for active workers in your pool to restore consistent shard ownership.
- Enabled additional tracing for prefix cache hits/misses and captured log snapshot (attached).

What we are doing next (short-term roadmap)
- Engineering is building a patch that replaces the reclaim path with a two-phase handoff to ensure prefix cache flush happens before new worker accepts in-flight sessions (ETA: 72 hours).
- We will schedule a controlled maintenance window to apply the patch to your Dedicated pool; this will be a rolling update with health checks and expected <5m per shard disruption. Proposed window: May 6 02:00–04:00 UTC — please let me know if that conflicts.

Customer question we want to address now
- Any concerns about data exposure? Short answer: our logs and traces show no exfiltration and no request bodies were written to other tenants; we will include the verification traces in the final packet.

Attachment: larkspur-interim-log-snapshot.txt (short dump of critical traces around 02:14 UTC)

I will follow up with the completed RCA and a controlled rollout plan. If you prefer, we can set up a 30-minute call this week to walk through the technical details with engineering.

Best,
Irene
Irene Choi
Head of Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
From: Samira Khan <samira.khan@larkspur.ai>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-02T08:41:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Interim findings on April 28th latency spike + immediate next steps

Thanks Irene — appreciate the quick update. A couple quick Qs:
- Please confirm explicitly that no PII or customer payloads were sent to other tenants.
- We need the exact minute-by-minute timeline for our compliance team — can you provide that in the final packet?
- Regarding credits: given the business impact to two of our customers during that 36-minute window, we will expect Redwood to include SLA remediation in the final communication.

We'll await the full RCA. A call is fine if that helps speed things up.

— Samira
Director, Platform Engineering
Larkspur AI
From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-03T14:05:00-07:00
Subject: FW: Interim findings — engineering short note (private)

Irene / Karthik — internal engineering note to line up the final RCA text for Samira. Paste of our condensed findings below (for inclusion in the customer-facing packet).

Technical root cause (concise)
- Trigger: autoscaler reclamation happened during a high-concurrency window. The reclaim path used a fast_reclaim flag that allowed immediate worker removal without waiting for KV prefix flush.
- Race: a new worker accepted the same model shard before residue prefix keys were invalidated; in a narrow timing window some requests used a mismatched KV namespace which returned stale tokenization state for certain prompt prefixes.
- Contributing factor: a kernel/driver update to our inference host image (2.4.1) changed thread scheduling timing, exposing the race.

Why this led to user-visible latency and 5xxs
- Stale KV reads caused additional fallback processing in the runtime (reconstruction of missing KV state) which adds tokenization and prefill latency. Under pressure, some requests timed out and surfaced 5xx.

Planned fix and rollout steps (owner assignments)
1) Short-term (this week) — disable fast_reclaim globally on Dedicated pools while we test the safer two-phase handoff. Owner: infra-oncall (David). ETA: done for Larkspur pool.
2) Code patch — introduce two-phase handoff + explicit cache invalidation barrier in reclaim path. Owner: runtime-team (Karthik). ETA: 72h smoke test + internal staged rollout.
3) Staged rollout — canary -> 10% -> 50% -> 100% of Dedicated pools with aggressive traces enabled and automatic rollback on anomaly. Owner: release-engineering (David + Karthik). ETA: 7 days from patch approval.
4) Verification & evidence pack — deterministic trace export for your compliance team, including minute-by-minute timeline and the specific request-ids impacted. Owner: reliability (Irene). ETA: included in final packet.

Compromise mitigation suggestion
- Offer a one-time SLA credit proportional to affected token consumption for the 36-minute window; legal/sales should confirm exact terms.

Irene — once runtime confirms the patch PR number I will draft the formal timeline table for Samira and attach the code PR and smoke test logs.

— David

On a side note: the kernel timing shift means we should also add a quick host-image test in our preflight to catch scheduling-sensitive races. Karthik, can you own that follow-up?
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
To: Samira Khan <samira.khan@larkspur.ai>
Cc: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Larkspur Support <support@larkspur.ai>
Date: 2027-05-08T09:05:00-07:00
Subject: Final RCA, timeline, and action commitments — Larkspur April 28 event

Hi Samira and team,

Attached is the final RCA packet (larkspur-rca-timeline.pdf) and a short mitigation checklist (mitigation-checklist.csv). Below is a condensed, customer-ready summary and the specific action commitments we will execute.

Executive summary (one paragraph)
On 2027-04-28 at ~02:14 UTC a race in our worker reclaim path caused temporary prefix KV inconsistencies when model shards were reallocated. Those inconsistencies led to additional runtime reconstruction work for a subset of in-flight requests, increasing latency and producing a small number of timeouts (5xx). We consider this a reliability regression introduced by the interaction of a reclaimed-worker optimization (fast_reclaim) and a host image timing change.

Minute-by-minute timeline (high level)
- 2027-04-28 02:13:42 UTC — Autoscaler initiated reclaim on node x-17 due to transient load spike.
- 02:14:08 UTC — First elevated latency observed by synthetic monitors.
- 02:14:40–02:50 UTC — Elevated latency & 5xx peak affecting ~1.8% of requests across your pool.
- 02:16:30 UTC — On-call disabled fast_reclaim on the affected pool (mitigation).
- 02:30:00 UTC — Coordinated drain+rehash completed; error rate returned to baseline.

Root cause (technical)
- A race condition allowed new workers to accept a model shard before the previous worker had completed KV prefix invalidation. The fast_reclaim optimization skipped the barrier. A host-image timing change made the window large enough to impact in-flight traffic.

Remediation & commitments (owners + ETA)
- Immediate: fast_reclaim disabled globally on Dedicated pools until rollout completes. Owner: infra (David). Status: completed.
- Code patch: implement two-phase handoff + explicit prefix invalidation barrier in reclaim path. Owner: runtime (Karthik). ETA: May 5 (completed smoke tests), PR: #5982.
- Staged rollout: canary -> 10% -> 50% -> 100% with automatic rollback and smoke checks. Owner: release-engineering (David + Karthik). ETA: May 8 (rolling complete).
- Verification packet: minute-by-minute request-id export and trace assertions for all impacted request-ids. Owner: reliability (Irene). ETA: included in this packet.
- Prevent recurrence: add host-image scheduling test into preflight and add a reclaim race detector in unit/integration tests. Owner: core infra (Karthik). ETA: June 1.

Impact assessment & SLA remediation
- Verified customer-visible errors: brief window (36 minutes), limited to a subset of requests. No evidence of data leakage; traces and request payload checks are attached.
- Compensation: we propose a one-time SLA credit covering consumption during the impact window; our Sales/Finance contact will follow up with the credit calculation.

What we want from you
- Please confirm the maintenance window preference if you want us to schedule a short rolling verification update during a low-traffic window.
- If you require a call to review the attached traces line-by-line, we can set that up — suggested slots: May 9 14:00–15:00 UTC or May 10 10:00–11:00 UTC.

Attachments: larkspur-rca-timeline.pdf (full packet), mitigation-checklist.csv (action checklist), larkspur-interim-log-snapshot.txt (initial traces)

Again, I apologize for the disruption and we are committed to making this right. If you have immediate concerns, reply and I will escalate to our incident exec on-call.

Best regards,
Irene Choi
Head of Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
